policy.row_policy: Every upstream result is applicable_candidate or excluded with a reason; validation or performance failure never deletes a row.
policy.publication_policy: Candidate status is not execution evidence. Publication requires exact suite, engine, adapter, executable, environment, raw samples, failures, skips, outputs, and timed boundaries.

maintenance.claim_boundary: Diagnostic peak-throughput corroboration only; never a modern-web or broad-representativeness claim.

assessment.determinism: The pinned base harness resets Math.random to its deterministic generator before each suite; individual timing scores remain sampled performance data.
assessment.workload_coverage: Legacy compute, object, RegExp, compiler, emulator, and generated asm.js peak-throughput workloads; no modern modules, async applications, or browser loading stack.
assessment.run_duration: Unmeasured until the owned adapter completes full exact-output validation on each engine.

adapter.anti_specialization: Attribution-only diagnostic pairs exact sources with a deterministic leading-comment variant applied after pinned-byte SHA-256 validation; scored sources remain untransformed.
adapter.timed_boundary: The upstream BenchmarkSuite timing and score boundary remains unchanged; process wall/CPU/RSS are additional outer measurements.
adapter.output_contract: Retain each named upstream result and final suite score; do not use the aggregate to hide a row.

The embedded jsbn and base64 components need a file-level SPDX and notice audit before evidence is retained.
The source says MIT-style but does not carry an exact SPDX license; provenance must be resolved before selection.
The generated Scheme2JS source has no file license header in the pinned tree.
The first subset does not yet specify GPL notice retention or validate the bundled mock-DOM output boundary.
The generated asm.js provenance, latency score, and exact output oracle need an owned validation fixture.
The multipart GPL workload and conditional browser paths need notice packaging and an exact shell-path audit.
Embedded Closure and jQuery-derived sources need a complete license inventory and the eval/global output needs an owned oracle.
Generated Emscripten provenance, the data payload, and the exact output oracle need an owned validation fixture.
The embedded compiler/input license notices, compilation output, and eval boundary need an owned validation fixture.

maintenance.claim_boundary: Inventory only; the alpha suite is not selected and produces no zig-js result.

assessment.determinism: Not yet audited per subtest; the upstream driver controls iterations and scoring.
assessment.workload_coverage: Current JavaScript and WebAssembly suite with browser and shell modes; exact applicable subtests are unresolved.
assessment.run_duration: Unmeasured because no subtest is selected.

adapter.output_contract: No result is accepted until every selected upstream subtest and score component is inventoried.

rows.exclusion_reason: The pinned alpha tree has mixed per-workload licensing, npm preparation, compressed assets, and an unresolved exact shell subtest inventory.

evidence_contract.aggregate_policy: Every applicable row remains visible beside any official or geometric aggregate.
evidence_contract.host_adapter_policy: Adapters may provide documented shell globals and result capture only; they may not rewrite workload logic, inputs, iteration counts, timing, or expected output.
evidence_contract.termination_policy: The isolated zig-js harness uniformly sets its evaluation-step budget to unsigned-64 maximum for every row and mode; the collector's retained per-child external process timeout owns termination.
evidence_contract.recognizer_policy: A static engine-source scan rejects suite revisions, hashes, and distinctive identifiers; exact and source-hash-mutated attribution children must pass identical output contracts and select identical nonzero execution-tier and bytecode-admission sets.
evidence_contract.engine_isolation: Each engine executes in a separate process and executable; zig-js exports never interpose on another engine.
evidence_contract.checkpoint_policy: The collector atomically replaces an artifact outside the zig-js worktree after every child process, preserving raw stdout, parsed JSON when available, stderr, exit status, timeout state, and contract validation.
evidence_contract.dispersion_policy: Only contract-valid passed score children contribute statistics; failed and invalid children remain retained and identified beside the valid-only dispersion.
evidence_contract.aggregate_failure_policy: No selected-subset geometric aggregate exists until collection is complete and every applicable row passes.
evidence_contract.publication_policy: Suite-specific evidence requires at least seven score samples per row, a complete all-passing matrix, and an explicitly selected quiet reference host on AC power; otherwise the artifact is diagnostic.
